festivals.name: ALTAVAS STO. NIÑO FESTIVAL
festivals.description: It is the day that signifies the end of the Fil-American war in the Municipality of Altavas. From then on, January 22 has become the official date of celebration for the town’s Annual Thanksgiving and Armistice Day. Later, the date was adopted as its municipal town fiesta. This is the continuation of the joyous celebration of peace upon the conclusion of the war that took place in the said town.

festivals.name: Santo Niño Festival
festivals.description: Altavas celebrates the Santo Niño during its town fiesta. The town’s observance also commemorates a local armistice linked to the Philippine-American War. January 22 became the date of thanksgiving and remembrance and was later adopted as the town fiesta date.

attractions.name: HISTORICAL MARKER OF GENERAL ANANIAS DIOKNO
attractions.description: The late General Anianas headed the expedition force in Panay in 1899. He was captured in Barangay Dalipdip, Altavas, Aklan during the Philippine-American war in 1901. In recognition of his gallantry and contribution to the katipunan, he was recognized by the Altavas Historical Research Society, Incorporated (AHRS) as a valued historical property of Altavas, Aklan.

attractions.name: Tinagong Dagat
attractions.description: Tinagong Dagat lies between Altavas and Batan. Two islets partly screen it from Batan Bay, and mangroves and rocky stretches line the shore. The provincial tourism profile describes the inlet as about eight kilometers long and four kilometers wide.

Altavas is blessed with natural resources and scenic attractions, potential as tourist destinations once fully developed. Barangay Talon as the name suggests is home to several water falls and even caves. “Talon” means water falls in English. Agtutoe-an and Quinasay-an Water Falls are both found in Barangay Talon. Kipot and Suhot caves are also situated in the same district. Kipot is a local term that means “narrow” while suhot means “to pass through.” Macawiwili Falls on the other hand is in Barangay Cabugao.

attractions.name: Macawiwili Falls
attractions.description: Natural site named in the provincial tourism profile. The recorded location is Cabugao. The town’s January Santo Niño celebration is tied to a local armistice observance.

products.description: Puto Seko is a dried rice cake delicacy made only in this town.

products.name: Nito bags
products.description: Nito bags is nito handicrafts listed in municipal tourism inventory. The recorded location is Brgy. Cabugao. The town’s January Santo Niño celebration is tied to a local armistice observance.

products.name: Puto Seko
products.description: Puto seko is named in the provincial tourism profile as a local product; source naming differs from Puto Tostado references. The town’s January Santo Niño celebration is tied to a local armistice observance.

products.name: Puto Tostado
products.description: Puto Tostado is a toasted rice cake documented in Altavas. UP Visayas cultural mapping describes a recipe handed down within a local family and a preparation method that uses charcoal. The toasted cake is one of the foods associated with the municipality.

products.name: Virgin coconut oil
products.description: Virgin coconut oil is sAMAKA community-produced virgin coconut oil listed in the municipal tourism inventory. The town’s January Santo Niño celebration is tied to a local armistice observance.

overview.text: An inland municipality in eastern Aklan, formerly called Jemino and renamed in honor of Senator Jose Altavas. Local tourism materials highlight its upland landscape, waterfalls and caves. The town’s January Santo Niño celebration is tied to a local armistice observance. Outside the town center, Barangay Talon has waterfalls and caves, while Tinagong Dagat lies along the boundary with Batan. Altavas is also associated with toasted rice cakes and nito handicrafts.

festivals.name: Enchanting Balete
festivals.description: Annual civic and religious town fiesta named by the provincial tourism profile. The recorded location is Balete town. Agtawagon Hill and the Kabuhi-an Center reflect different sides of local life, from the landscape to community livelihood.

festivals.name: Kultura Balete
festivals.description: Kultura Balete presents local culture and arts as part of the municipality’s civic calendar. The provincial tourism profile associates the program with Culture and Arts Month and the Enchanting Balete festival. Activities have been reported in February and October.

attractions.name: Agtawagon Hill
attractions.description: Agtawagon Hill is hill attraction identified in the municipal tourism profile. Cultural celebrations include Enchanting Balete and Kultura Balete.

attractions.name: Basura Garden
attractions.description: Garden attraction; privately operated according to tourism profile. Agtawagon Hill and the Kabuhi-an Center reflect different sides of local life, from the landscape to community livelihood.

attractions.name: Kabuhi-an Center
attractions.description: Kabuhi-an Center is community and visitor center listed in the tourism profile. Cultural celebrations include Enchanting Balete and Kultura Balete.

products.description: Agricultural and fishery of which the most notable are piña cloth, nito craft, pinipig, rambutan, oysters, crabs, prawns (both brackish and freshwater).

products.name: Limbok
products.description: Limbok is a traditional Balete delicacy made from fresh, mature glutinous rice. UP Visayas documented the practice in Sitio Bangbang, Barangay Feliciano, where it forms part of the community’s knowledge of preparing rice by hand.

products.name: Nito crafts
products.description: Nito crafts is nito-based crafts listed among Balete products. Agtawagon Hill and the Kabuhi-an Center reflect different sides of local life, from the landscape to community livelihood.

products.name: Piña cloth
products.description: Aklan piña textile and related craft product featured in the provincial tourism profile. The recorded location is Balete / Aklan. Agtawagon Hill and the Kabuhi-an Center reflect different sides of local life, from the landscape to community livelihood.

products.name: Pinipig
products.description: Pinipig is pounded young rice listed as a local product. Agtawagon Hill and the Kabuhi-an Center reflect different sides of local life, from the landscape to community livelihood.

products.name: Rambutan
products.description: Rambutan is seasonal fruit listed as a local product. Agtawagon Hill and the Kabuhi-an Center reflect different sides of local life, from the landscape to community livelihood.

overview.text: A municipality known for its agricultural and coastal setting and community tourism initiatives. The official provincial profile presents local cultural, hill and garden attractions. Agtawagon Hill and the Kabuhi-an Center reflect different sides of local life, from the landscape to community livelihood. Cultural celebrations include Enchanting Balete and Kultura Balete. In Feliciano, local makers prepare limbok from glutinous rice.

festivals.name: Saguibin Festival
festivals.description: Community festival whose name is associated with helping one another. The recorded location is Banga town. Manduyog Hill and the main campus of Aklan State University are among the town’s prominent landmarks.

festivals.name: Pag-Aeaw-Aeaw
festivals.description: Remembrance/re-enactment associated with the Banga Crossing massacre. Manduyog Hill and the main campus of Aklan State University are among the town’s prominent landmarks.

attractions.name: AKLAN STATE UNIVERSITY(ASU)
attractions.description: is the oldest agricultural school in Aklan. ASU is considered as one of the institutions of learning in Western Visayas. It started as the Banga Intermediate School in 1917 through a resolution passed by the Provincial Board headed by Governor Simeon Mobo. The school became a farm school with the conversion of the Banga Intermediate School into the Capiz Farm School (Aklan being a part of Capiz then), which was formally opened in June 1918.

attractions.name: Manduyog Hill
attractions.description: Manduyog Hill rises above the Aklan State University campus in Banga. Life-size Stations of the Cross mark the path up the hill, linking the landscape to a local tradition of religious devotion.
attractions.location: Aklan State University Main Campus, Banga

products.name: Calamansi
products.description: Farm produce purchased from Banga farmers by the provincial government in 2020; listed as agricultural produce, not as a unique specialty food. Manduyog Hill and the main campus of Aklan State University are among the town’s prominent landmarks.

overview.text: An inland municipality in central Aklan whose local identity includes the Banga Crossing remembrance and community cooperation themes. Manduyog Hill and the main campus of Aklan State University are among the town’s prominent landmarks. The Saguibin Festival draws on the idea of helping one another, while Pag-Aeaw-Aeaw remembers the events at Banga Crossing.

festivals.name: BATAN ATI-ATI MALAKARA FESTIVAL
festivals.description: The participants celebrating this festival put on paper mache masks matching prepared costumes. The festival is observed in honor of the Sto. Niño with merriment and street dancing along the streets and plaza of the town center for an abundant harvest, prosperity and peace. A holy mass is celebrated on Sunday morning prior to opening the contest proper in a parade of participating tribes.

festivals.name: JUEZ DE CUCHILLO
festivals.description: This annual celebration is observed in commemoration of the 74 Batangnons who were ruthlessly mass murdered in the hands of the Japanese invaders on the fateful day of October 19, 1942. Highlight activities include a commemorative mass offering, civic parade and program located at the actual site of the so-called massacre, and the re-enactment of “Juez de Cuchillo”.

attractions.name: Kalantiaw Shrine
attractions.description: Historic site associated with the Kalantiaw story. NHCP has delisted the Code of Kalantiaw marker because the code has no valid historical basis; present the site as a physical landmark only. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao.

attractions.name: Ob-Ob Hill
attractions.description: Ob-Ob Hill is hill viewpoint and natural attraction listed in the municipal tourism profile. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao.

attractions.name: PRISTINE BEACHES OF BARANGAY SONGCOLAN, MANDONG, NAPTI AND MAMBUQUIAO
attractions.description: Stretches 10 kms. more or less from Barangay Songcolan, Mandong Napti and Mambuquiao. Resto bars, and other facilities and amenities along the the vast expense of Batan Bay, Tinago Lake, Sibuyan Sea offer a relaxing hideaway from the hustle and bustle routines. More so, Mambuquiao has a marine protected area and fish sanctuary. Locally called pito, it has the highest live coral cover in Salian Bay and is ideal for people who enjoys snorkeling and scuba diving.

attractions.name: Camanci Falls
attractions.description: Camanci Falls is falls listed among the municipality’s natural attractions. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao.

attractions.name: ANGAS WHITE STONE MOUNTAIN
attractions.description: The place is suited for trekking and mountain climbing. Known to locals as “Puting Bato,” it is also a protected area for wildlife. Puting Bato is the habitat of rare species and mammals, birds, wild flowers and endangered species.

attractions.name: Pandan Hills
attractions.description: Pandan Hills is upland attraction listed in the municipal tourism profile. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao.

OUR LADY OF THE IMMACULATE CONCEPTION PARISH CHURCH (Eastern Side) – The parish church in Poblacion was established by the Spanish colonizers and friars during the colonization and evangelization of Batang (Batan) and Philippine Archipelago on December 8, 1702 hence considered one of the oldest churches in the province. Nuestra Señora De Immaculada Concepcion was enthroned and venerated in the church of Batang in honor of His Majesty King of Spain. The church celebrated its quadri-centennial (400 years) of parish existence in 2002.

attractions.name: Batan Sea Port
attractions.description: Batan Sea Port is in Poblacion, near the center of this coastal municipality. The provincial tourism profile identifies it as one of Batan’s historic transport landmarks. It offers a point of reference for understanding the town’s connection to Batan Bay.

attractions.name: San Lorenzo Ruiz de Manila Parish Church
attractions.description: Parish church dedicated to San Lorenzo Ruiz. The recorded location is Camaligan. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao.

attractions.name: CORAL GARDEN
attractions.description: Located in the coast of Barangay Mambuquiao, this garden consists of 170.5 hectares of marine waters and a reserve area of 709 ha. Within the fish sanctuary is the “pito” reef, which is the feeding, spawning and nursery area of commercially important species of fish. It covers a wide expanse of coral reefs about one (1) kilometer from the shoreline of the barangay northward. In this protected area by virtue of Municipal Ordinance No. 2001-02, various kinds of coral formations of different colors can be found.

attractions.name: OLD SPANISH RELICS
attractions.description: From the Spanish colonization period, cannons, distilleries and old cemeteries with brick facade can be seen in Batan.

attractions.name: Mambuquiao Beach
attractions.description: Mambuquiao Beach is beach destination listed in the provincial tourism profile. The recorded location is Brgy. Mambuquiao. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao.

attractions.name: Mandong Beach
attractions.description: Mandong Beach is beach destination listed in the provincial tourism profile. The recorded location is Brgy. Mandong. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao.

attractions.name: Napti Beach
attractions.description: Napti Beach is beach destination listed in the provincial tourism profile. The recorded location is Brgy. Napti. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao.

attractions.name: Songcolan Beach
attractions.description: Songcolan Beach is beach destination listed in the provincial tourism profile. The recorded location is Brgy. Songcolan. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao.

products.description: Batan makes this special puto or steamed rice cake of several different flavors such as cheese and buko. A good idea for snacks, it is about 6-8 inches in diameter, big enough to fill the stomachs of a small group.

products.name: Puto buko
products.description: Batan’s puto buko is a coconut-flavored version of the town’s steamed rice cake. The provincial tourism profile also identifies a cheese variant and describes the cakes as large enough to share.

products.name: Puto cheese
products.description: Batan’s puto cheese is a cheese-flavored steamed rice cake. It is one of the versions made locally, alongside a coconut-flavored puto. The provincial tourism profile describes the cakes as large enough to serve several people.

overview.text: A coastal municipality with historical heritage sites and beaches. NHCP documents Batang as an early trade center/seat; the separate Kalantiaw-code claim has been formally delisted. The coast includes beaches in Songcolan, Mandong, Napti and Mambuquiao. Mambuquiao also has a protected coral area. The town celebrates Ati-Ati Malakara, and local makers prepare steamed puto in flavors such as cheese and coconut.

festivals.name: Panagat Festival
festivals.description: Buruanga’s Panagat Festival celebrates fishing and the people whose livelihoods depend on the sea. The municipality showcases its fish products during the festivities, connecting the town’s coastal identity with the importance of caring for marine resources.

attractions.name: Ingus-Ingus Hill
attractions.description: Ingus-Ingus Hill overlooks the coast of Buruanga and was used as a lookout during the Spanish colonial period, according to the provincial tourism profile. A cave lies below the hill. Local stories connect the cave with raiders who targeted ships carrying valuable cargo.

attractions.name: Ashram Balay Pagduaw
attractions.description: Ashram Balay Pagduaw is a retreat site in Buruanga. Its purpose is quiet reflection and spiritual retreat in a natural setting. It is among the municipality’s faith-related destinations.

attractions.name: SAINT ANTHONY OF PADUA PARISH CHURCH
attractions.description: A century-old religious edifice, this church is the center of worship of Buruanganons for their Patrons, Saint Anthony and Nuestra Sra. De Salvacion.

ARIEL’S POINT (formerly Batasan Point) – Touted as the best dive site in Aklan, it has cliff diving sites overlooking turquoise swimming holes, and lush mangrove. Recently featured in Cosmopolitan magazine & TripAdvisor as top Boracay attraction. It is a good stopover for scuba divers, snorkelers, and cliff-board divers for its rich marine life.

attractions.name: Sabang Cave
attractions.description: Sabang Cave occupies an elevated site in Buruanga. From the area around the cave, the coast opens into views of beaches and the sea. The cave is one of several coastal and limestone features identified in the provincial tourism profile.

attractions.name: Sapsapon Cave
attractions.description: Sapsapon Cave in Buruanga is known for its stalactites and stalagmites. These formations develop as minerals carried by dripping water build up on the cave ceiling and floor. The cave shows another side of a municipality better known for its coastline.

attractions.name: Tigis Falls
attractions.description: Tigis Falls is waterfall attraction listed by the municipal tourism profile. The Panagat Festival celebrates fishing, and in Bagongbayan, fish drying on rocks is a documented local practice.

attractions.name: Talisay Beach
attractions.description: Talisay Beach is beach listed in the provincial tourism profile. The Panagat Festival celebrates fishing, and in Bagongbayan, fish drying on rocks is a documented local practice.

attractions.name: HINUGTAN WHITE BEACH
attractions.description: This is a perfect place for snorkeling and diving. For adventurous visitors, Hinugtan White Beach provides a multitude of pleasurable experiences in which they can explore the underwater world.

attractions.name: Tuburan Baybay
attractions.description: Tuburan Baybay is coastal area listed in the tourism profile. Its shoreline includes Hinugtan and Talisay beaches, while Sabang and Sapsapon caves and Tigis Falls show the variety of its inland and coastal terrain.

attractions.name: Pagatpat Mangrove
attractions.description: Pagatpat Mangrove is mangrove site listed as a nature attraction. Its shoreline includes Hinugtan and Talisay beaches, while Sabang and Sapsapon caves and Tigis Falls show the variety of its inland and coastal terrain.

attractions.name: Hacienda Maria
attractions.description: Hacienda Maria in Buruanga is a nature property with caves and waterfalls. The provincial tourism profile also describes demonstrations of how lambanog is made. Its attractions bring together the area’s landscape and a local coconut-based tradition.

attractions.name: Ariel’s Point
attractions.description: Ariel’s Point, formerly known as Batasan Point, is a coastal site in Buruanga. Cliffs overlook clear swimming areas and patches of mangroves. The site is associated with cliff diving and snorkeling, and the surrounding waters support marine life.

attractions.name: Pagbulad sa Bato
attractions.description: In Barangay Bagongbayan, Buruanga, fishers use rocks as a surface for sun-drying fish. The practice is known as pagbulad sa bato. UP Visayas documents it as part of the coastal community’s food knowledge and fishing livelihood.

attractions.name: St. Anthony Church
attractions.description: The Saint Anthony of Padua Parish Church is a longtime center of worship in Buruanga. Local religious life honors Saint Anthony and Nuestra Señora de Salvación. The parish church is a landmark in the town center.

products.name: Bukarilyo
products.description: Bukarilyo is bukarilyo listed among Buruanga fair products. Its shoreline includes Hinugtan and Talisay beaches, while Sabang and Sapsapon caves and Tigis Falls show the variety of its inland and coastal terrain.

products.name: Buri bags
products.description: Buri bags is buri-weaving products reported at a provincial tourism fair. Its shoreline includes Hinugtan and Talisay beaches, while Sabang and Sapsapon caves and Tigis Falls show the variety of its inland and coastal terrain.

products.name: Fresh fish and seafood
products.description: Fishing and seafood are part of the municipality’s coastal livelihood and festival identity. The recorded location is Buruanga coast. Its shoreline includes Hinugtan and Talisay beaches, while Sabang and Sapsapon caves and Tigis Falls show the variety of its inland and coastal terrain.

products.name: Puto
products.description: Puto is puto listed among Buruanga fair products. Its shoreline includes Hinugtan and Talisay beaches, while Sabang and Sapsapon caves and Tigis Falls show the variety of its inland and coastal terrain.

overview.text: A coastal municipality at the northwestern end of Aklan, with beaches, hills, caves, waterfalls and fishing communities. Its shoreline includes Hinugtan and Talisay beaches, while Sabang and Sapsapon caves and Tigis Falls show the variety of its inland and coastal terrain. The Panagat Festival celebrates fishing, and in Bagongbayan, fish drying on rocks is a documented local practice.

festivals.name: IBAJAY ATI-ATI MUNICIPAL AND DEVOTIONAL FIESTA
festivals.description: This is a yearly religious event observed as a mark of respect for the town’s patron saint Sto. Niño. The festival is being symbolized by the transferring of the image of the Holy Child from where it was originally discovered to the church to be witnessed by the devoted Catholics.

attractions.name: KATUNGGAN IT IBAJAY
attractions.description: The Bugtongbato-Naisud basin (inland) mangrove boasts 27 mangrove species. It is the only mangrove community in the country that comprises 77% of the total 35 Philippine species. It has been identified and acknowledged by SEAFDEC-AQD as an ideal site for its various scientific researches on mangrove and aquaculture. With its high level of biodiversity, giant and century-old endemic mangrove species of natural growth will entice eco-tourists to explore what they think is impossible to discover.

attractions.name: Campo Verde
attractions.description: Nature attraction near the Tangalan boundary. The recorded location is Ibajay–Tangalan boundary. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education.

ALEJANDRO MELCHOR’S BIRTHPLACE – Ibajay is where a renowned Filipino in history who was distinguished for his work on bridges. Alejandro Melchor (1900-1947) was a civil engineer, mathematician, and educator who functioned as the Secretary of National Defense under President Manuel Quezon. But Melchor’s major claim to fame was designing the pontoon bridges recognized to have contributed much to winning the Second World War for the Allied Forces.

attractions.name: Ibajay Beach
attractions.description: Coastal visitor area along the municipality’s shoreline. The recorded location is Coastal barangays of Ibajay. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education.

attractions.name: IBAJAY RIVERS
attractions.description: The massive Ibajay River, transversing the Municipality from the farthest barangay of Yawan to the mouth of the River at Poblacion, is pompous of its clear and surging waters which had created gigantic and mystic boulders along the way challenging bamboo rafters in shooting its rapids and dubious currents-offering great adventures for water sports enthusiasts and eco-tourists.

attractions.name: IBAJAY FALLS
attractions.description: One of Ibajay’s waterfalls is Snibaa Falls, a fine veil of white reachable after a brief mountain hike. Its cold waters can recharge you after a day’s worth of exploring.

attractions.name: Alejandro Melchor birthplace
attractions.description: Birthplace/heritage site associated with Filipino engineer and public official Alejandro Melchor. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education.

attractions.name: Ibajay River
attractions.description: Ibajay River is river attraction included in the provincial tourism profile. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education.

attractions.name: Katunggan mangrove area
attractions.description: Katunggan It Ibajay protects a mangrove forest in Ibajay, Aklan. Elevated walkways bring visitors into the forest, where they can see mangrove roots and learn about the plants that support coastal wildlife. The site combines habitat conservation with environmental education.

attractions.name: Snibaa Falls
attractions.description: Snibaa Falls is waterfall attraction listed in the municipal tourism profile. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education.

products.description: Ibajay is famous for its nito handicraft made particularly in Barangay Mabusao, Regador and San Jose and has already become an export potential. Pottery has been a traditional industry of Barangay Coloncolong and their intricately-designed jars, vases, flower pots, and bricks have attracted traders, tourists and commuters along the National Highway where their products are displayed. A sumptuous ”linumak” commonly prepared in the households is now commercially available. Pulvoron and other native delicacies are becoming popular as gifts and “pasalubong” abroad.

products.name: Coloncolong pottery
products.description: Coloncolong pottery is traditional pottery identified in local tourism materials. The recorded location is Brgy. Coloncolong. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education.

products.name: Linumak
products.description: Linumak is local sticky-rice delicacy listed in the provincial tourism profile. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education.

products.name: Nito crafts
products.description: Nito-based handicrafts produced in Mabusao, Regador and San Jose. The recorded location is Barangays Mabusao, Regador and San Jose. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education.
products.location: Barangays Mabusao, Regador and San Jose

products.name: Pulvoron
products.description: Pulvoron is local delicacy listed in the provincial tourism profile. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education.

overview.text: A northern coastal municipality known for its coastline, river and mangrove areas, with local craft and food traditions. At Katunggan It Ibajay, boardwalks cross a mangrove forest protected for conservation and education. The municipality also has a devotional Ati-Ati celebration, pottery in Coloncolong and nito handicrafts in several barangays.

festivals.name: KALIBO STO. NIÑO ATI-ATIHAN FESTIVAL
festivals.description: This festival dates back when the peace agreement between early Negrito settlers and the Maraynons that came over from Borneo was being commemorated. Therefore, participants willingly blacken themselves with soot and put on colorful tribal costumes. Nowadays, it is one of the most vibrant celebrations honoring the Holy Child Jesus, Sto. Niño. Hence, it is considered as the Filipino Mardis Gras. Known to be “The Mother of all Philippine Festivals,” there are many activities and events that people are looking forward to during the week-long celebration. Some activities include the Search for Mutya ag Lakan it Kalibo Ati-atihan, Aklan Festivals Parade, Higante Contest and concluded every 3rd Sunday of January with a High Mass to kick off the final day of merrymaking and procession. The key activity and one of the main reasons tourist travel many miles to Kalibo is the native dance competitions of participating tribes in full gear accompanied by primitive rhythm of drumbeats. More so, what makes this festival more exciting is that everyone, not only the competing groups, is allowed to crowd the principal streets of Kalibo to dance nonstop for several days rejoicing zealously to their religious vows.

festivals.name: XIX MARTYRS OF AKLAN
festivals.description: It is commemoration of the 19 martyrs of Aklan who consecrated their lives in the cause of freedom from their colonizers. This is held every 23rd of March.

festivals.name: AKLAN DAY CELEBRATION
festivals.description: An annual celebration held in the Provincial Capitol Grounds commemorating the province’s Founding Anniversary on April 25th, formally declaring independence from its mother province of Capiz in 1956.

festivals.name: AKLAN PIÑA AND FIBER FESTIVAL
festivals.description: A week-long festival simultaneously held during the province’s founding anniversary celebration on the 25th of April each year. It is a product showcase of world class craftsmanship and ingenuity using indigenous raw materials such as abaca, piña fiber, raffia. The festival aims to promote, preserve and develop the loom-weaving industry in the province, hoping to establish Aklan as the handloom-weaving destination in the country.

festivals.name: Kalibo Food Festival
festivals.description: Kalibo Food Festival is food event listed in the provincial tourism calendar. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

festivals.name: Higante contest
festivals.description: Large-figure contest held as part of town festivities. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

festivals.name: Feast of St. John the Baptist
festivals.description: Religious feast and community observance. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

festivals.name: Kalibo Day
festivals.description: Town anniversary events. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

festivals.name: Iwag it Kalibonhon
festivals.description: Seasonal community celebration and lights/event program. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

festivals.name: Piña / Fiber events
festivals.description: Events celebrating Aklan piña and fiber craft, associated with Kalibo’s founding anniversary period. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

attractions.name: AKLAN FREEDOM SHRINE
attractions.description: It is dedicated to the 19 martyrs of Aklan who initiated the revolt against Spain. Hence, the street where the shrine stands is named X1X Martyrs Street.

attractions.name: Tigayon Hill and caves
attractions.description: Hill, caves and viewpoint destination. The recorded location is Tigayon, Kalibo. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

attractions.name: Museo it Akean
attractions.description: Museum documenting Aklan history and culture. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

attractions.name: Piña Village
attractions.description: Craft area associated with piña-fiber weaving. The recorded location is New Buswang, Kalibo. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

attractions.name: Ati-Atihan Village
attractions.description: Cultural and visitor site associated with Ati-Atihan traditions. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

attractions.name: Kalibo Cathedral
attractions.description: Major church and town landmark. The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers.

attractions.name: Bakhawan Eco-Park
attractions.description: Bakhawan Eco-Park in New Buswang, Kalibo, grew out of a mangrove reforestation project. The forest is both a coastal habitat and a place to learn about mangroves. It gives visitors a view of Kalibo’s coastal environment beyond the town center.

products.description: Piña; fiber made from the leaves of a pineapple plant was a textile unique to the Philippines and is deemed as “The Queen of Philippine Fabrics.” Consequently, Aklan has become the prime producer of piña cloth in the country. The piña cloth and other piña products could cost a fortune when exported abroad and are considered works of art and could count for one’s collector’s items. Nowadays, international designers use pineapple fabric for their fashion line as well.

Kalibo’s sweet longganisa has made its mark to people from nearby cities and provinces. Province visitors considers their trip incomplete not having to bring home such food products. Other processed meat products that Kalibo is famous for are Chorizo, Tocino and Embutido.

Barbecue stalls on several streets in town offer wide varieties of Barbecue products. Compared to other cities and provinces however, one that is noticeably different in these stalls in Kalibo would be “bread” to be barbecued as well.

products.name: Kalibo longganisa

The town is a center for the Santo Niño Ati-Atihan celebration and for weaving cloth from pineapple fibers. Visitors can learn about provincial history at Museo it Akean or see the mangrove forest at Bakhawan Eco-Park in New Buswang.

attractions.description: Lezo is a small town, but there are still more than a couple of things to see. First, pay the Lezo Plaza a visit. It is home to most events of the municipality and you will surely see kids of locals playing basketball. Tennis and badminton courts are also available for those who want more physical activity. The Town Hall is situated beside the church, and is a new building. You can go in and up the stairs to the balcony to have a view the whole plaza and other municipal buildings. Just down the road from the plaza is the Church of the town, a beautiful old building. For the brave ones, a climb up the Bell town to see a nice panoramic view of the town is worth a try. Beside the Church is the Lezo Pottery where locals make beautiful clay pots and finish them in their kiln. At the pottery, you can ask if you can try your luck making something. As in most small towns, a walk around is the best thing to do to explore and interact with the locals, who are always friendly and accommodating.

attractions.name: Church and bell tower

Residents living by the river bank make their living making clay pots and jars likewise using indigenous materials found abundant in their area. Buying directly from the pot makers will save you some amount, hence the town is being visited for these beautifully hand-made pots. Meanwhile, the pop-rice squares or better known locally as “ampaw” is made of cooked dried rice, deeply fried, sugar coated, subsequently molded or cut into desired sizes and dried until crispy.

Its preparation uses tapay, a fermentation ingredient, and families associate the dish with occasions such as All Souls’ Day, Christmas and New Year.

Pottery is one of Lezo’s defining crafts, with local makers shaping earthen pots and jars. The plaza, church and bell tower mark the town center. UP Visayas also documents inumoe, a fermented rice delicacy associated with holiday gatherings.

The town is also a major producer of rice, cattle, bananas, copra, vegetables, bamboo, root crops, and fruits such as lanzones, durian, marang, mangosteen, seedless pomelo, chico, rambutan, and local oranges. This municipality can potentially produce high-value crops, tropical flowers and vegetables as well.

attractions.name: LIKITINON WHITE ROCKS
attractions.description: These are beautiful labyrinth of bone-white boulders, grottoes and stone bath tubs sculpted by crystalline water gushing through the virgin jungle valley traversing one of the cleanest inland bodies of water in the country, the Timbaban River in Ma. Christina.

attractions.description: Discover the unspoiled and panoramic scenic view of Panipiason, while you are strolling the amazing hanging bridge. Strutting along bridge is something that locals highly recommend. The man-made hanging bridge is perfect for picnic goers. A certified adventurer’s playground, the Panipiason hanging bridge is Madalag’s only hanging bridge.

products.description: Madalag basically has an agricultural economy. Over 7,000 hectares of the municipality land is devoted to agriculture. Farming and home industries are the key source of livelihood for its people. Most if not all the twenty five (25) barangays grow rice while corn is planted in several upland areas. Other crops grown in this town include pineapple, camote and ube. Fruit trees such as lanzones, rambutan, marang and commercial crops like coconut and abaca are also produced. The mountainous and hilly parts are where high valued forest products such as narra, acacia, and mahogany and minor products like buri, rattan, bamboo, nipa sap and firewood are produced.

products.name: Chicharon

products.name: Tinuom
products.description: Madalag is known for tinuom, a local dish prepared with chicken and rice in a leaf wrapping. The wrapping holds the ingredients together as they cook and is part of the dish’s presentation. The dish also gives its name to the municipality’s Tinuom Festival.

overview.text: An upland municipality with river, rock and waterfall attractions and a food tradition associated with tinuom. Liktinon White Rocks in Maria Cristina and the hanging bridge in Panipiason are among the town’s distinctive places. The municipality is also associated with tinuom, a leaf-wrapped chicken and rice dish that gives its name to the local Tinuom Festival.

festivals.description: MAKATO Sr. Sto. Niño Ati-atihan Festival – Historically, the Ati-atihan Festival of Makato started prior to the coming of the Spaniards sow the seeds of Christianity into this land. For the duration of the celebration, a huge count of Catholic devotees from everywhere in the country and the world is beckoned to come and join in the uplifting festivity and spiritual avidity of gratefulness to Sto. Niño. The image of the Holy Child Jesus is brought out of the church and is carried around the town. The image is escorted by street dancers who perform to the beat of drums and other instruments. The dancers are dressed in eye-catching costumes of striking colors. It is celebrated every 3rd Friday of January and throughout that day, there are several masses carried out that people can attend. The church also conducts baptisms during the celebration.

festivals.name: Sto. Niño Ati-atihan

attractions.name: Aklan Sports Complex

The town of Makato has several areas which, when fully developed, would lure in visitors, both local and foreign. These are the “Salimuno falls” at Barangay Libang which is roughly 7 kilometers away from the town center and is can be easily reached when traveling by land. Even during dry season, crystal clear water cascades incessantly that dipping into it is irresistable. Tourists will surely enjoy its refreshing effect. The other prospected spot is the Baybay beach. It is situated about 8 kilometers from the Poblacion via Barangay Albasan of Numancia and is accessible only by land transportation. Upon completion of the Hagachac-Alibagon Bridge, travel time would be reduced to just around ten minutes at minimum.

In Makato stands one of the Aklan State University (ASU) campuses which originally served as an extension high school, and was hence named the ASU Annex. As of 2006, the campus is home to the Teacher Education Center (TEC), and occupies 10 hectares in Barangay Castillo.

festivals.description: MALINAO Ati-Atihan Festival – One of the esteemed elders of the town, who also was significant in the founding of the parish of Malinao in 1796, Capitan Simon Enriquez commanded the mission of saving Fr. Fernando Legaspi, parish priest of Malinao, as the latter was captured by lurking pirates, the Moros. The highly respected priest was on his way to attend the feast of Sto. Niño in the town of Ibajay. Father Legaspi was only released in exchange of gold and he considered the incident a miracle and particularly attributed it to the Sto. Niño of Ibajay. In gratitude, he later instigated an act of devotion to the Holy Child by means of fasting and other penitential rites that is still being followed through this festival by the people of Malinao today. This festival is celebrated every 3rd Friday of January.

festivals.description: “PACTO DE SANGRE” OR BLOOD COMPACT – New Washington is best known in the province for the Blood Compact Celebration or the Pacto de Sangre in Spanish. This annual tradition held every March 1 to 3 has been a significant part in the municipality’s history. The celebration is done in commemoration of the Aklanon heroes who have sacrificed their own lives just to liberate fellow Filipinos from the colonization of the Spanish forces. The Pacto De Sangre happened in Sitio Kuntang of Barangay Ochando in New Washington on March 23, 1897. The Aklanon Katipuneros, namely Romualdo Dalida, Isidro Jimenez, Cornelio Delfin, Valeriano Dalida, Benito Motus, Albino Rabaria, Teodorico Motus and Juan Dalida fought the Spanish regime to uphold the freedom and independence the Filipino people were battling for. Each of the Katipuneros voluntarily wound their wrists and used their blood in signing the document detailing their grievances as a symbol of their revolt against the then Spanish authorities. Furthermore, this blood compact has also been a considered as a symbolism of eternal friendship and brotherhood. The pact was then remembered as one of the most important events in Philippine history and inspired the annual ceremony of commemorating the Blood Compact in the small town that is New Washington.

festivals.name: Pacto de Sangre commemoration
festivals.description: New Washington commemorates the Pacto de Sangre, an episode in the local history of the Philippine Revolution. The National Historical Commission of the Philippines places the historic blood compact at Sitio Kuntang in Barangay Ochando on March 2 and 3, 1897.

attractions.name: THE JAIME L. SIN MONUMENT
attractions.description: This bronze life-size representation of Jaime L. Sin is a present to the people of New Washington, Aklan from Ambassador Antonio L. Cabanguan Chua. He was one of the Cardinal’s dearest friends and supporters. The donor chose to mark the Cardinal’s 73rd birthday, August 30, 2007 with the solemn unveiling of his 22 feet high monument the next day that same year in recognition of his honor at his hometown. Throughout his lifetime, Cardinal Sin was a gift of God and at the same time, a hero to the Filipino people whom he served with love and devotion.

attractions.name: ISLA KAPISPISAN

This bird sanctuary is a project initiated by the College of Fisheries & Marine Sciences in New Washington. It is a mangrove forest that provides habitats to different aquatic species, birds and other associated organisms.

products.description: New Washington also has a lot to offer when we talk about food. Among the regulars are seafood such as crabs and prawns at their best. Sea shell locally known as “hale-hale” is also available and is a legendary aphrodisiac. For the adventurous, eating a local delicacy called “tamiluk” would be a great experience. Tamiluk is a wood worm that feed on dead mangrove trees. There is also another worm locally called “sasing” which is a marine worm dug from the inter-tidal zone of the Lagatik river and is eaten raw. These worms are not for the squeamish and the faint hearted. Some consider them exotic and some taboo.

Among the common “kakanins” is the glutinous rice (malagkit) cooked in coconut milk and wrapped in coconut fronds locally called “ibos”. This is unique to the town as it can also be found in other towns and even in other parts of the country but some give it a twist of their own usually in the way it is wrapped. Other local snacks are the “suman” and “amboeong”.

There is an exotic drink popular in the Visayas called “tuba”. This is a form of coconut wine. Fresh “tuba” has wine like smell but milder (compared to red wine from fermented grapes) and taste like one but sweeter. The sweetness and sourness however would depend on some factors particularly the age of the coconut tree. “Tuba” does not keep long as it readily ferments to vinegar. One to two days old “tuba” already tastes sour. It should be enjoyed fresh from the coconut tree.

overview.text: A coastal municipality with fishing livelihoods and a historic Pacto de Sangre site in Ochando. The Lagatik River and the coast are part of the town’s fishing and seafood economy. The Pink Sisters Convent is in Polo, while Ochando is associated with the 1897 Pacto de Sangre. Local foods include crabs, prawns and rice delicacies such as ibos and suman.

festivals.name: Lechon Parade
festivals.description: Numancia’s Lechon Parade celebrates roast pig as part of the town’s food culture. The event brings attention to local lechon makers and their craft. Pork liempo from Bulwang is another food associated with the municipality.

attractions.name: NAHAUNANG ATIS (FIRST AETAS)
attractions.description: Another worthwhile stop over is a visit to the oldest aeta village in the province located in Bulwang near the Aklan River bank.

attractions.name: CLUSTERED CENTURY-OLD ACACIA TREES
attractions.description: Get enchanted while being surrounded with fourteen century-old giant trees (from originally 17 trees) planted in 1892 in clusters. These giant rain trees (English name of Acacia) are standing tall and proud for 119 years within the Albasan Elementary School.
Beaches of Barangays Camanci and Navitas are also worth the visit.

products.description: Numancia is dubbed as the home of the most mouthwatering and best tasting lechon in the province. There is also an establishment in Barangay Bulwang that offers the best pork liempo which has become famous to both locals and people from nearby cities and provinces. Visitors usually drop by to buy some for take away.

overview.text: A municipality near Kalibo with agricultural sites, heritage trees and coastal barangays. The Lechon Parade celebrates a food tradition associated with the municipality. Camanci and Navitas are coastal destinations, while Albasan Elementary School has historic acacia trees. Bulwang is associated with pork liempo and is home to an Ati community.

festivals.description: Bugna Festival is town festival listed in the provincial tourism calendar. Jawili Falls flows through seven natural basins near the coast.

festivals.name: HEROES OF VIVO TANGALAN
festivals.description: Held every July 31, this annual event commemorates the triumph of then local residents of Barangay Vivo in the municipality of Tangalan from Spanish colonizers. It was said the local residents plotted against the Spaniards in a dinner intended for the latter and massacred them all upon having been caught drunk in the feast.

attractions.name: Afga Wave Rock Formation
attractions.description: Coastal rock formation shaped by wave action. The recorded location is Afga. Jawili Falls flows through seven natural basins near the coast.

attractions.name: ST. JOHN NEPOMUCENE PARISH CHURCH
attractions.description: It is a century old church designed with limestone wall similar to the beautiful Miag-ao Church of Iloilo. After 28 years of forced labor, the construction of the church was completed in 1889. Women, as much as men and children were encouraged to join this so-called great polo and toiled from sunrise to sunset carrying blocks of corals and limestone from the quarries in Barangay Afga to the construction site in the town center. The church building is among the oldest religious edifices in the province.

attractions.name: Jawili Falls
attractions.description: Jawili Falls in Tangalan is a series of cascades that flow through seven natural basins. The pools and rocky setting make the falls one of the municipality’s most recognizable natural landmarks. Jawili Beach is in the same barangay.

attractions.name: Jawili Beach
attractions.description: Coastal beach destination near Jawili Falls. Jawili Falls flows through seven natural basins near the coast.

attractions.name: JAWILI MANGROVE FOOTWALK
attractions.description: The mangrove footwalk is an added attraction for visitors in Barangay Jawili. It is a mere few minutes walk from Jawili Falls and it takes you through a lush and diverse mangrove environment. There are over twenty species of mangroves in the area, two of which are internationally rare.

attractions.name: Campo Verde
attractions.description: Nature attraction in Panayakan. Jawili Falls flows through seven natural basins near the coast.

attractions.name: MARINE SANCTUARY AND CORAL GARDEN
attractions.description: The 375 hectare Marine Sanctuary was officially established in 2003 at Pungtod Reef. Numerous species of hard and soft rock corals, sponges, shells, sea stars, sea cucumber, oysters and lobsters can be found within the sanctuary. There are varieties of colorful fish as well including Butterflyfish, Anglefish, Damselfish, Parrotfish, Surgeonfish, Scorpionfish and Sweetlips among others. Endangered sea snakes and sea turtles are also found within the sanctuary, as well as dolphins and stingrays.

attractions.name: Pungtod Reef marine sanctuary

overview.text: A coastal municipality with a rocky shoreline, waterfall pools, mangroves and marine conservation areas. Jawili Falls flows through seven natural basins near the coast. The rock formations at Afga, mangrove walkways and Pungtod Reef highlight the town’s shoreline and marine habitats. The St. John Nepomucene Church is a landmark in the town center.
